intro: A decoder can train on a mixture of previous gold tokens and previous model predictions. Make the choice with supplied random draws so behavior is reproducible.
task: Build decoder input tokens, beginning with a start token and then selecting the previous gold or predicted token.
requirements: targets, predictions and draws are matching batch-by-time matrices; time>=2. Token IDs are integers 0..1000000. draws lies in [0,1), teacher_probability in [0,1], and start_id is an integer token ID.

Return a batch-by-time integer array. Column zero is start_id. For t>=1, use targets[:,t-1] when draws[:,t-1]<teacher_probability and predictions[:,t-1] otherwise. The final column of each supplied matrix is not used as a previous token but must still satisfy validation.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Choose the previous token before shifting it into the next input position.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: At probability zero use predictions everywhere after the start; at one use gold tokens everywhere.

explanation: Scheduled teacher forcing changes which historical token the decoder receives during training. This addresses the difference between training with correct histories and generating from its own earlier predictions.
Supplied predictions are treated as fixed data here. A live autoregressive rollout would recompute later predictions after each chosen input, which is outside this deterministic batch transformation.
